column1: # renames.tsv — THE RENAME REGISTRY. One row per rename this plugin has made.
# WHY IT EXISTS: renaming used to cost a manual sweep plus a migration note somebody
# had to remember (`renamed_from:` on a routine template; a hard-coded `guides|policies|
# specs` branch in layout-doctor.sh; two migrations named literally in converge-layout.sh).
# Six renames in eight days each paid that price, and a consuming repository holding an
# old name met a floor written for a shape it had never had, with no statement of what
# the name became. A rename now costs ONE ROW HERE.
# FORMAT: tab-separated, five columns, no quoting. Blank lines and lines starting with
# `#` are ignored. Read it ONLY through list-renames.sh — two hand-rolled parsers drift
# exactly as four hand-rolled frontmatter readers once did.
#   kind   `area` | `name`. Two kinds and no third.
#   old    the name as it was. For `area`, a .workaholic/ top-level directory name
#          (bare, no slash). For `name`, the token as it is written (`housekeep`,
#          `workaholic:report`, `/report`).
#   new    the name as it is now. NEVER empty — see "a retirement is not a rename".
#   since  YYYY-MM-DD, the day the rename landed.
#   why    one short clause. An issue number is ideal; a reader who meets the old name
#          in the wild gets this sentence and nothing else.
# THE TWO KINDS ARE THE WHOLE DESIGN, and the line between them is not negotiable
# downward:
#   `area` is MECHANICAL. A .workaholic/ top-level directory is a machine-owned path
#          with exactly one correct destination, so migrate-renamed-areas.sh `git mv`s
#          it and rewrites the machine-read occurrences of the old path INSIDE
#          .workaholic/. Nothing else.
#   `name` is PROPOSED, never applied. A name appears in prose a human wrote, in a
#          consuming repository's own documents, and in vocabulary that may deliberately
#          differ. rename-conversions.sh finds the survivors and PRINTS a bulk conversion
#          command the operator runs or declines. This repository's standing rule is that
#          everything needing a judgment is reported with the decision it needs and never
#          guessed (converge-layout.sh's header); a script that rewrote `report` to
#          `story` across somebody's documents would be exactly the act that rule refuses.
#          `report` is also an ordinary English word — a blind sed here is the failure
#          mode, which is why this half proposes.
# A RETIREMENT IS NOT A RENAME, and does not belong here. .workaholic/guides/,
# policies/ and specs/ were DELETED on 2026-08-13 (issue #436); their content had no
# destination. A row with an empty `new` would make the column's meaning conditional and
# would need a "skip if empty" branch in the migration — a second behaviour inside one
# kind. layout-doctor.sh keeps its own `retired-area` classification for those three,
# which is a fixed historical fact about three names rather than a growing list.
# THIS IS A MIGRATION RECORD, NOT HISTORY. A row is DELETED once the fleet has cut over,
# on the same reasoning that deletes `renamed_from:` from a routine template: it
# describes a migration, not a name. Left forever, the table becomes a changelog nobody
# prunes and every doctor run searches for names no repository still holds. Git history
# is the durable record of what a thing used to be called.
